coverage.API-001: Public Go SDK calls real HTTP handlers for the Session lifecycle, inspection, Event cursoring, cancellation, close, Artifact reads, and Approval commands; the standalone binary and disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO/Temporal composition pass.
coverage.API-002: The public SDK import graph and independent temporary consumer compile exclude implementation adapters and retain only runtime-owned public types and errors.
coverage.API-004: Public HTTP/SDK lifecycle tests cover same-request replay, conflicting reuse, expiry, and scoped receipt lookup.
coverage.API-005: Public HTTP/SDK authorization matrix checks authenticated same-tenant and cross-tenant non-enumerating denial across catalog and owner routes.
coverage.API-006: Public request and Event limits, SDK response and Artifact limits, and malformed JSON fuzzing are bounded before runtime dispatch.
coverage.API-007: Public HTTP/SDK Event tests cover ordered replay, duplicate-tolerant resume, and explicit Gap after compacted cursor history.
coverage.API-008: A dropped public observation is replayed without cancelling accepted work; explicit cancellation and durable cancellation control are separately exercised.
coverage.API-009: Raw authenticated Session inspection JSON contains no forbidden backend execution-ID field names.
coverage.API-010: The public SDK refuses an unconfigured logical model profile; raw HTTP refuses a provider credential-shaped field without echoing it.
coverage.API-011: The v1 OpenAPI compatibility baseline, generated route-table drift check, temporary GOWORK=off consumer compile, and migration policy are exercised.
coverage.API-012: Public HTTP/SDK tests prove immutable Agent/Policy lifecycle and separate tenant-admin versus ordinary Session authority.

limitations: API-003 remains unpromoted because this artifact has no current-SHA documentation publication or HTTPS proof.
The temporary GOWORK=off consumer check uses the candidate module replacement; it is not an immutable remote release-tag or external-consumer proof.
The standalone and PostgreSQL/MinIO/Temporal dependencies are disposable integration fixtures, not protected production operations.
This evidence does not execute a live model provider, external sandbox command, Firecracker, or Linux KVM environment.
